about: Class types and their blocks. Only Flow is switched on. Block order never changes. Block minutes come from timing templates and must add up to the class length.

classTypes.label: Flow
classTypes.description: Eleven blocks in four sections, same order every time. The exercises change.

peakBlock.note: The peak pose goes near the end of the full body block, in Functional.

blocks.label: Footwork
blocks.purpose: Warm up legs and feet. Heels, arches, toes, close or wide, parallel or turned out, full range, halfway, pulses.

blocks.label: Bridge
blocks.purpose: Back body. Hinge or articulated bridges. Flows straight on from reformer footwork.

blocks.label: Abs and supine arms
blocks.purpose: Abdominal work, and supine arms (lying on the back, arms in the straps or with light weights).

blocks.label: Plank
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Plank holds and plank variations. Level 1 on the mat or forearms on the box, Level 1.5 adds the reformer.

blocks.label: Lower body
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.

blocks.label: Upper back
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Pulling work: chest expansion, biceps, rows.

blocks.label: Upper front
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Pressing and front of the shoulders: serve a tray, presentation, hug a tree, salute.

blocks.label: Side body and rotation
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Side bending, side-lying work and rotation.

blocks.label: Full body
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Whole body work. The peak pose lands here, near the end.

blocks.label: Back extension
blocks.note: Block names and order from Jay. Minutes inside the section are an assumption.
blocks.purpose: Lying face down or kneeling back extension.

blocks.label: Stretch
blocks.purpose: Release what was worked and finish calm and tall.

timingTemplates.name: Standard
timingTemplates.note: Section minutes from Jay (15, 18, 12, 5). Footwork, bridge and abs from Jay. The split inside Strength and tone and Functional is an assumption.

timingTemplates.name: Gentle pace (older clients)
timingTemplates.note: Longer footwork and a little more strength work, less full body. Sections stay inside Jay's ranges.

timingTemplates.name: More strength and tone
timingTemplates.note: Strength and tone at Jay's top of 20, Functional at 10.

timingTemplates.name: More full body
timingTemplates.note: Functional at Jay's top of 15, Strength and tone at 15.

scoring.about: Soft rule weights. Higher means the generator cares more. All are assumptions to tune with Jay. Equipment change cost is multiplied by the client group's pace factor, so older classes change equipment less. jayOverused weighs down the exercises Jay called overused. supineArms nudges one supine arms exercise into the abs block. positionChange is the cost of moving the client to a new position, scaled per level. skillBonus favors the coordination, balance and stability work Jay wants at Level 1.5.

range.note: 10 to 15 minutes. Full body and back extension appear only here.

overusedByJay.note: Supine arms lower and lift, triceps press, abduction and arm circles. Weighted down hard but still possible. Prefer fresh supine arms options.

minMinutes.note: Smallest a block can be on the timing screen.

maxMinutes.note: Largest a block can be on the timing screen.
